The first is some minor field line movement near the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-06-26T17:48Z. The second candidate is near-continuous activity and fluctuation from AR 14478 that is best seen in SDO AIA 193 for hours prior to and following the CME start time.

There is also some field line movement likely associated with this dimming over the S limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-26T20:06Z and in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-06-26T19:49Z. A much less likely source candidate for this CME is associated with a C2.4 class flare from AR 14475 (S09W04) that peaked at 2026-06-26T20:21Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131, but the eruption followed by some post eruptive arcades is best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 195.

It may be visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 over its west limb starting 2026-06-27T15:05Z, but this is quite early. This CME exhibits possible deflection from the source location due to its proximity to a coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. The leading edge is not clearly measurable in GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

data.note: CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and NW in STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. Also observed here in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2026-06-29T11:05Z. This source timing is early, but slow to evolve, so still a good candidate that aligns with triangulation. Partially overlapped by following CME 2026-06-29T17:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2, and faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2. Likely observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 at 2026-06-29T17:15Z as a brief dimming and field line movement near the NW limb from STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, and the very faint front in SOHO LASCO C2 better observed in running difference imagery.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-06-29T19:38Z. The source is associated with an M1.4 class flare from AR 14479 peaking at 2026-06-29T21:40Z observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed in SDO AIA 171/193 as brightening, field line movement, and slight dimming following the flare. The CME front appears deflected slightly NE from the source region.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis as SOHO LASCO C2. Using the source location at N16W04, we find the front deflected NE, and without the ability to triangulate in real-time. As such, this region's eruptive history is referenced, and a latitude of N30 then fitting the longitude to E03 is used to approximate the parameters, and may vary as a result. This deflection does fit with the observed wide opening field lines in SDO AIA 193.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption from Active Region 14479 (N16W15) starting around 2026-06-30T13:30Z which exhibits northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is observed northeast of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Full halo CME currently observed only in GOES CCOR-1 and somewhat blocked by its pylon. Not yet observed in other coronagraphs due to a SOHO LASCO DSN gap between 2026-06-30T20:15Z to 2026-06-30T23:45Z, and STEREO A data gap starting at 2026-06-30T19:23Z. The source is associated with an X1.1 flare (N17W18) observed in SDO AIA 131 from AR 14479 (N16W22), peaking at 2026-06-30T20:50Z. Also observed as a NE-deflected EUV wave and wide swath of dimming in SDO AIA 193/211 centered around N20W05, brightening/flare ribbons along a channel to the NE of the region in SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304, and a post-eruptive brightening starting around 2026-06-30T21:46Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary shock analysis with only several available GOES CCOR-1 frames. Due to the limited frames and full halo presentation, the shock width could vary, impacting speed. This is enough to use COR2 to estimate the more northward latitude than preliminary analysis and estimate the half width, while no frames are officially included in the analysis.

The source of this CME(s) is an eruption from the area of Active Region 14485 (S10W34) starting around 2026-07-09T06:56Z to the SW in GOES SUVI 195 with additional eruption signatures to the NW of AR 14485 (S10W34) in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2026-07-09T07:08Z. These eruptions are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 and 304 as well as in SDO/AIA wavelengths following an eclipse.
